??? question "Which extra line on a diagnostic can point at a second, related place, such as an earlier declaration?"

    A note. It helps explain why the primary span is wrong.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md).

??? question "Which tool joins object files and the runtime library into one executable?"

    The linker. It fills in each name with the address of the code it refers to.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "In which style of IR is every named value assigned exactly once, so that a changing variable becomes a series of versions?"

    Static single assignment (SSA) form.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "What do we call the kind of machine and operating system a generated program is meant to run on?"

    The target. The back end produces code for it.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "Which compiler stage links each use of a name to its declaration and reports unknown or duplicate names?"

    Name resolution. Its problems are reported as name errors.

    Introduced in [4. Names and scopes](stage-4-names-and-scopes.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../../specification/declarations.md#37-name-resolution).

??? question "In v0.1, what does it take for two types to be compatible?"

    Being the same type, because v0.1 has no automatic conversions.

    Introduced in [5. Types and language rules](stage-5-types-and-rules.md).

??? question "Which part of the compiler reads the tokens, checks them against the grammar and builds a syntax tree?"

    The parser. It reports a syntax error when the tokens do not fit the grammar.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md). Specification: [11. Formal grammar](../../specification/grammar.md).

??? question "In SSA form, what picks which version of a value to use at a point where two paths meet?"

    A phi. Its choice depends on which path was taken.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "Which text stream does a program write to by default, and which tests capture to compare with the expected output?"

    Standard output.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "Which kind of test passes only if the compiler rejects a bad program for the right reason at the right place?"

    A negative test.

    Introduced in [5. Types and language rules](stage-5-types-and-rules.md).

??? question "Where does the code for `print` come from in a compiled Vortex program?"

    From the runtime library, code supplied with the language that generated programs call for services such as printing.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "Which diagnostic category covers an unknown name, a duplicate in the same scope, or a named type that does not resolve?"

    A name error.

    Introduced in [4. Names and scopes](stage-4-names-and-scopes.md). Specification: [10. Diagnostics](../../specification/diagnostics.md#name-error).

??? question "What do we call one possible route through a function body, following one choice at every `if`, loop and `return`?"

    A control-flow path. A non-`void` function must return a value on every reachable one.

    Introduced in [5. Types and language rules](stage-5-types-and-rules.md).

??? question "What is the readable text form of machine instructions, which an assembler turns into machine code?"

    Assembly language.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "Which compiler stage works out the type of every expression and checks that operations, calls and returns fit together?"

    Type checking. For example, it rejects `3.0 & 1.0`, because bitwise operators need integers.

    Introduced in [5. Types and language rules](stage-5-types-and-rules.md). Specification: [12. Glossary](../../specification/glossary.md).

??? question "What kind of rule, such as an index being inside its array, depends on values known only while the program runs?"

    A dynamic rule. Unless the compiler can prove the answer, it keeps a runtime check for it.

    Introduced in [5. Types and language rules](stage-5-types-and-rules.md). Specification: [1. Conformance and terminology](../../specification/conformance.md#14-static-and-dynamic-rules).

??? question "Why can a struct field named `x` and a local variable named `x` exist together without clashing?"

    The field names form their own namespace, reached only through a value of the struct type.

    Introduced in [4. Names and scopes](stage-4-names-and-scopes.md).

??? question "What are the small, very fast storage slots inside the processor called?"

    Registers. Instructions mostly work on values held in them.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "What do we call the written rules for which token sequences form valid programs?"

    The grammar. For Vortex it is the formal grammar chapter of the specification.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md). Specification: [11. Formal grammar](../../specification/grammar.md).

??? question "In `print(width)`, what is this appearance of `width` called, as opposed to the place where it was declared?"

    A use. Name resolution links each use to its declaration.

    Introduced in [4. Names and scopes](stage-4-names-and-scopes.md).

??? question "Which half of the compiler turns a checked program into code for a particular machine?"

    The back end. Another kind of machine, such as a GPU, would need another back end but the same front end.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "Which checks run after parsing to enforce rules that need context, such as `break` appearing only inside a loop?"

    Semantic analysis. It covers mutability, control-flow placement and entry-point validation.

    Introduced in [5. Types and language rules](stage-5-types-and-rules.md). Specification: [10. Diagnostics](../../specification/diagnostics.md#semantic-error).

??? question "What do we call the outside programs, such as an assembler and a linker, that the compiler depends on?"

    The toolchain.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "What do we call a variable declared with `let` inside a function?"

    A local variable. It needs an initializer and is visible from its declaration to the end of its block.

    Introduced in [Learn: 4. Variables and types](../../language-tour/04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../../specification/declarations.md#35-local-variable-declarations).

??? question "What is one basic operation a processor can carry out, such as adding two numbers, called?"

    An instruction. Machine code is a sequence of instructions in numeric form.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "What do we call a program that satisfies every applicable v0.1 rule?"

    Well-formed. A conforming compiler must accept it, within its documented limits.

    Introduced in [5. Types and language rules](stage-5-types-and-rules.md). Specification: [1. Conformance and terminology](../../specification/conformance.md#12-programs).

??? question "What do we call a word such as `let`, `fn` or `while` that the language reserves and that cannot be used as a name?"

    A keyword. Matching is case-sensitive, so `String` is a keyword but `string` is an identifier.

    Introduced in [2. The lexer](stage-2-lexer.md). Specification: [2. Lexical structure](../../specification/lexical-structure.md#24-keywords).

??? question "What do we call one trip over the whole program by one part of the compiler, doing one job?"

    A pass, such as checking types or lowering to IR.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "What do we call a program that reads source code, checks it, and writes out code a machine can run?"

    A compiler. It also rejects programs that break the rules and explains the problem.

    Introduced in [Overview](index.md).

??? question "What do we call a message from the compiler about a problem in the source?"

    A diagnostic. In v0.1 every diagnostic is an error and carries a source location.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md). Specification: [10. Diagnostics](../../specification/diagnostics.md#101-required-diagnostic-data).

??? question "What do we call simple instructions that are run by a virtual machine rather than directly by the processor?"

    Bytecode. Vortex compiles to machine code instead.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "What is it called when the compiler rewrites the checked syntax tree as a list of small, ordered steps?"

    Lowering. It moves the program toward a more machine-like form, such as an IR.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md). Specification: [12. Glossary](../../specification/glossary.md).

??? question "What is the compiler's record of which names are declared in which scopes called?"

    The symbol table. It is an idea, not a particular data structure.

    Introduced in [4. Names and scopes](stage-4-names-and-scopes.md).

??? question "What do we say about a declaration whose name can be used at a given point in the program?"

    It is visible at that point. Outside its scope it is not.

    Introduced in [4. Names and scopes](stage-4-names-and-scopes.md).

??? question "What do we call the period while the finished executable is running?"

    Run time. Checks that depend on values known only then are made at run time.

    Introduced in [Learn: 8. Runtime and numerical rules](../../language-tour/06-runtime-and-numerical-rules.md). Specification: [12. Glossary](../../specification/glossary.md).

??? question "Which tree keeps only the meaningful parts of a program and drops punctuation whose job the tree's shape already shows?"

    The abstract syntax tree (AST), which the guide simply calls the syntax tree.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md). Specification: [12. Glossary](../../specification/glossary.md).

??? question "How does the compiler find the declaration that a use refers to?"

    By lookup, starting in the use's own scope and moving outward.

    Introduced in [4. Names and scopes](stage-4-names-and-scopes.md).

??? question "What does the specification call checking the grammatical structure of a token stream and building the AST?"

    Parsing, the job of the parser.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md). Specification: [12. Glossary](../../specification/glossary.md).

??? question "What kind of rule can the compiler check just by reading the program, such as a type or mutability rule?"

    A static rule. Breaking one is reported before the program runs.

    Introduced in [5. Types and language rules](stage-5-types-and-rules.md). Specification: [1. Conformance and terminology](../../specification/conformance.md#14-static-and-dynamic-rules).

??? question "What do we call the form of the program inside the compiler that is no longer source text but not yet machine code?"

    The intermediate representation (IR). It sits between the front end and the back end.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "What sorts diagnostics into kinds such as lexical error or type error, and how many kinds does the specification list?"

    The category. The specification lists eight.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md). Specification: [10. Diagnostics](../../specification/diagnostics.md#102-categories).

??? question "What do we call a file of machine code that is not yet a complete program and may refer to code elsewhere, such as `print`?"

    An object file. A linker joins object files and libraries into an executable.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "What is the process that turns the compiler's own source code into the `vortex` program called?"

    The build. The build system is the tool that knows the recipe.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "What do we call a file of machine code that the operating system can start as a program?"

    An executable. The linker produces it from object files and libraries.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "Which compiler step turns `[f32; 2 + 2]` into `[f32; 4]` before the program runs?"

    Constant evaluation. Array dimensions are the v0.1 case that needs it.

    Introduced in [5. Types and language rules](stage-5-types-and-rules.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../../specification/arrays.md#72-dimension-rules).

??? question "Which half of the compiler reads the source, works out what it means and rejects bad programs?"

    The front end. In this guide it is stages 1 to 5.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "Which style of compiler design uses many very small passes, each performing a single task?"

    Nanopass.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "What is source that breaks at least one required language rule called, and what must the compiler do with it?"

    Ill-formed. The compiler must reject it.

    Introduced in [5. Types and language rules](stage-5-types-and-rules.md). Specification: [1. Conformance and terminology](../../specification/conformance.md#13-implementation-conformance).
